subject: Hosted API pricing: minimum spend, burst safeguards, and overage proposal
body:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@ariasys.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-01 09:12 AM (PDT)
Subject: Hosted API pricing: minimum spend, burst safeguards, and overage proposal

Hi Maria —

Great speaking earlier. Attached is a concise pricing worksheet and a proposed commit tier that maps to Aria's expected Q1‑Q4 usage profile. High level:

- Annual commit: $120k (equivalent to ~600M tokens at our Tier 2 per-token rate)
- Committed per-token rate: $0.00018/token for generation, $0.00012/token for embeddings
- Soft-burst allowance: 30% monthly above committed throughput at the committed rate (for up to 2 months per quarter)
- On-demand overage: billed at 1.9x the committed per‑token rate by default; discounts to 1.5x when quarterly true‑up thresholds met
- Quarterly true-up: reconciles usage, applies excess usage credits if commit exceeded

Attachments: 20261001-redwood-pricing-sheet.pdf (worksheet).

Questions I wanted to flag for you now so we can converge quickly:
- Does Aria need firm minimum monthly spend for finance/forecasting, or is an annual minimum acceptable?
- Do you require burst credits (one‑time buffer for first two months) or prefer automatic on‑demand throttles?

Happy to align on a short mutual action plan and get legal a first SOW draft.

Best,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
+1 415‑555‑0182

From: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@ariasys.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@ariasys.com, Daniel Park <daniel.park@ariasys.com>
Date: 2026-10-02 11:45 AM (PDT)
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing: minimum spend, burst safeguards, and overage proposal

Thanks Jonas — appreciate the quick turnaround. A few clarifying items from procurement and platform:

1) Minimum spend: finance prefers a predictable monthly floor we can forecast to our execs. Is there a way to split the $120k into a monthly minimum ($10k/mo) that still preserves the annual incentive pricing?
2) Burst handling: we expect several product launch spikes where usage could be 4–5x baseline for short windows. We need:
   - A defined burst buffer that doesn't immediately trigger a punitive overage.
   - Clear rollback or fallback behavior (e.g., degrade at a lower model tier vs. unlimited overage).
3) Overage rate: procurement wants the on‑demand multiplier capped at 1.6x for the first two quarters, with a re‑negotiation clause thereafter.
4) SLAs: we need clarity on how SLA credits interact with true‑ups.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can offer a monthly minimum with a managed burst buffer and an initial capped overage multiplier? If so we can move to share a PO template and get legal involved.

—Maria
Maria Gonzalez
Head of Platform, Aria Systems
maria.gonzalez@ariasys.com

---

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-03 08:07 AM (PDT)
Subject: Fwd: Aria Systems — procurement asks on minimums & burst (need guidance)

Laura / Vivek — forwarding Maria's reply. They want: monthly floor, burst buffer for 4–5x spikes, and an initial cap on the overage multiplier (1.6x). Also ask how SLA credits interplay with true‑ups.

Can we propose an approach that balances revenue predictability with product protection (we don't want unlimited exposure)? I'm thinking:
- Convert annual commit to a monthly minimum ($10k/mo) with a front-loaded first quarter invoice if they prefer cash flow predictability.
- Soft-burst policy: allow 2x baseline auto at committed rate, then auto-failover to a lower-cost model tier for short sustained spikes; provide 2x burst credits per quarter that cover higher spikes without overage.
- Overage multiplier: propose 1.75x standard, reduce to 1.5x if they hit quarterly true-up thresholds. But Maria asked for 1.6x for first 2 quarters — can we do 1.6x limited-time?

Priyom, any constraints on billing system or legal we need to know?

Thanks,
Jonas

---

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-03 10:40 AM (PDT)
Subject: Re: Fwd: Aria Systems — procurement asks on minimums & burst (need guidance)

Team — quick ops note and recommended wording for the commercial summary:

Operational constraints:
- Our billing supports monthly minimums tied to an annual commit (we invoice monthly against the annual commitment). True‑ups are supported quarterly.
- Burst credits can be applied programmatically up to a configured token cap. We can provision 2x burst credits per quarter; additional burst usage moves to on‑demand overage.

Recommended commercial terms to propose to Aria:
1) Commit: $120,000/year with monthly minimum invoicing $10,000/mo.
2) Soft-burst: first 30% above committed baseline billed at committed rates; in addition Redwood will issue two one‑time burst credits per quarter covering up to an additional 40% each (only for the first 2 quarters after signature).
3) Overage: on‑demand billed at 1.6x the committed per‑token rate for the first two quarters post‑signature (per Maria's ask). Thereafter, standard overage is 1.85x unless a quarterly true‑up reduces it.
4) True‑up & credits: quarterly reconciliation; if actual usage > committed, the delta is billed at the applicable overage multiplier and applied to commitment for next quarter; if committed > actual, no refunds but credits can be carried for one quarter.
5) SLA interaction: SLA service credits apply independently; they do not offset token billing but will be paid as credits on the invoice if SLA triggers occur.

Legal notes: require a short redline to the SOW to add the burst credits clause and the temporary overage cap. We can do a 90‑day special concession schedule in the SOW (i.e., 1.6x cap for first two quarters).

I'll draft the redline and a PO‑friendly commercial summary for Jonas to send.

—Priyom
Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@ariasys.com>, procurement@ariasys.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-05 14:22 PM (PDT)
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing: minimum spend, burst safeguards, and overage proposal

Hi Maria / Aria procurement —

Thanks for the clear asks. Per internal discussion, here's a concise commercial summary and next steps (attached: 20261003-sow-draft.docx, 20261005-redline-terms.pdf):

Commercial summary (proposed):
- Annual commit: $120,000 (billed monthly as $10,000 minimum).
- Soft burst policy:
   • Committed rate applies to usage up to committed baseline +30% each month.
   • Redwood will issue two one‑time burst credits per quarter (covering up to an additional 40% each) for the first two quarters after signature to help with launches.
   • For sustained spikes beyond credits, Redwood will automatically fall back traffic to a compatible lower‑latency, lower‑cost model variant (customer can opt‑in to throttling instead).
- Overage pricing:
   • 1.6x the committed per‑token rate for the first two quarters after contract signature (temporary concession).
   • Thereafter, on‑demand overage is 1.85x unless reduced by quarterly true‑up.
- True‑up: quarterly reconciliation; billed delta at applicable overage multiplier; credits carry for one quarter.
- SLA: service credits applied per SLA incidents and show as invoice credits; SLA credits do not retroactively reduce token consumption billing.

Next steps:
1) If you agree, please confirm and we will:
   - Send an updated SOW + DocuSign envelope (link below).
   - Provide a PO template for your finance team.
2) Legal will accept limited redlines; anything material will route to our legal team for final review.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/flow/ARSIGN/ARIA-2026-007
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/ARIA-2026-007

If this aligns, we can aim to have a countersigned SOW within 7 business days and enable a staged onboarding plan.

Best,
Jonas
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

Attachment stubs: 20261003-sow-draft.docx (SOW draft), 20261005-redline-terms.pdf (redline showing burst credit clause and 2‑quarter overage cap).

From: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@ariasys.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@ariasys.com, Daniel Park <daniel.park@ariasys.com>
Date: 2026-10-05 17:38 PM (PDT)
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing: minimum spend, burst safeguards, and overage proposal

Jonas — this reads well and addresses the main concerns. Two quick follow ups before we route the PO:
1) Can you add an explicit example line in the SOW that shows how a 5x one‑week spike would be handled (we want predictable math for execs)?
2) Can you confirm onboarding timeline assumptions that come with the first two burst credit quarters (are credits available immediately after signature)?

If both are ok we'll route the PO and expect the DocuSign envelope.

I'll confirm internally once we see the updated SOW example. Thanks for pushing the temporary 1.6x concession — that will help us get this over the finance line.

—Maria
